verdict.tagline: Free cooperative store management blending chaotic expansion with early technical hurdles.
for_you_if: you want a free cooperative management game
you enjoy building and expanding a virtual supermarket
not_for_you_if: you plan to play on the Steam Deck
you encounter stability issues within the refund window
you dislike repetitive grind and missing mechanic explanations

distortion_flags.sentence: Reviews shift significantly from negative experiences within the refund window to high praise in later hours.

claims.claim: Reviewers encounter hackers in multiplayer sessions, though progress can be protected by backing up the day.

citations.review_text: I like the game, but hackers are problem. Fortunately you can backup your day :)

I largely write this review to balance all the positive reviews that can't bring themselves to say anything of value.

The game has a great foundation, great vibe and bug is free. You definitely get what you see in this game! Although that is also kind of the problem. There is very little beyond what you see, with the major problem being the lack of dynamics in the game. This leads to days quite quickly becoming identical to each other. And to top it off, the game is trivially easy and has no virtually punishment if you do manage to screw up.

TLDR my goal with this review is mainly to temper expectations for players and to hopefully get the developer to consider some gameplay changes to the game.

Still, if you like what you see and need some friendslop to play I ultimately do recommend that you try it.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that item quantities can disappear or decrease when placing stock onto shelves.

citations.review_text: There's a bug where your items disappear from the shelves when restocking. For example, I bought 2 boxes of cat food (20pcs each box, so a total of 40pcs) but when I placed it on the shelf, there's just 15 in total. It's the same with other items!

I think this game is super fun, its a little wonky in some aspects. These are just things I've noticed while playing the game and of course not really something I'd hope to be fixed right away. 
- The TV won't work in multiplayer with autosync. 
- The characters for "Chinese" are wrong. They're the characters for "Chinese" (the race) and not the language which is (中文). 
- And I also wished that there would be more decorations options like half walls, shelves (including better placement options for bigger products). 
- The AI on the restocking in storage could also be helped; if we could have a mechanic of the restockers using "overstock" boxes first.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that later gameplay becomes repetitive and grindy.

citations.review_text: So addictive for some reason. Later the gameplay can be insanely repetitive and AFKable tho... But somehow addictive

If you've ever looked at a supermarket and thought, "You know what? I want to spend hours stocking shelves instead of shopping," then this game is for you.

I've always enjoyed simulator games, and after a long break from the genre, this one was a nice surprise. Running your own store, managing inventory, expanding the business, and watching your tiny shop slowly turn into a supermarket is genuinely satisfying.

That said, the gameplay does get repetitive. You'll spend a lot of time restocking shelves, ordering products, and doing the same tasks over and over. Thankfully, the game keeps introducing new products, upgrades, and mechanics often enough to keep things interesting. It is a fairly long game, though, so be prepared for a bit of a grind.

The best part is that it's still in development. There's already a solid amount of content, and knowing that more features are on the way makes the experience even more promising.

Overall, if you're into simulator or management games, I'd definitely recommend giving it a try. Just don't be surprised when you start organizing virtual shelves better than the ones in your own kitchen.

Recommended.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that certain controls, such as how to change prices faster, are not explained anywhere in the game.

citations.review_text: Originally tried it because i didn't want to buy a million dollars worth of supermarket simulator DLC. But This one is great! Especially for being free. The cool pack with hats is great. Though some of the controls are  not easy to figure out. It never said anywhere you have to hold E to change the price faster, and had to look that up.

I will be willing to change my review to a positive (this game has potenital) but there are 2 major hurdles to this game right now that makes this kind of unplayable.

1. Every 7 in-game days you must manually check the price of every product and readjust them if the base price has increased. This is torture in a store 330+ products. (Realistically it was more around 100 by the time it became noticably tedious). There is an upgrade to automate it but it is only aunlocked at earliest in the midgame, and ONLY if you rush it. I rushed it and goit it around day 40? I had to afk a lot though... 

 I think a good compromise is to have an upgrade really early on that highlights prodcuts that have their prices updated, so you don't have to go through the tedium of having to manually checking every single product.


2. This stupid customer A.I. 
It is lategame day 82, diffuclty 10 and I have 10 shelves full of manufactored pies and they are in insane demand. On difficulty 2 I can easily sell 400+ pies in one day.  When the 1st shelf of pies are empty, instead of just moving on to the next shelf and grabbing a pie (like anyone would), but because the shelf is being restocked the customers instead wait for the shelf to be restocked. On the same shelf. Now imagine 30 customers standing around 1 shelf, waiting for pies to arrive. This caused a blob of people that essentially would not move, making it so that I had a customers in the store forever. 

Just come on, make it so that customers have no collision while shopping.

There are other bugs and jank as well, but those are easily fixed/workaroundable except these 2.

Otherwise, this game has potential, I look forward to chainging this review to a positive.
